label: copy-phase input s (fed-back s) early-to-mid in the copy, recall_idx 3-4 or 2 in short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass), never on original inputs or <DEL>, and only when the input token is a repeat (in_first=0). 93% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is s, meaning s was an original token at positions 1-4. The strongest activations (up to 3.7) are in very short sequences (L=3-4) where s is the second original token and is being fed back at recall_idx 2 (e.g. w s q <DEL> w [s]). Position dependence: at recall_idx 2, precision falls from about 0.9 at L=3-4 to under 0.1 at L>=7; recall_idx 3-4 gives 0.45-0.74 precision at every L; recall_idx 5 is weak (0.1-0.2); it is essentially silent at recall_idx >= 6 or near the end of long sequences. Weak firing on other fed-back letters (f, x, d, n, l) adds about 7% of mass. Even inside the predicate, about 40% of steps are inactive, and neither digit count nor first token explains which ones (dev F1 0.67, mass recall 0.87). The simpler predicate copy-phase in_tok==s with recall_idx 2-5 gets dev F1 0.56 and mass recall 0.93.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: s, f, x, d; t=12: s, f, x, d; t=11: s, f, x, n) and the token being output (most: q, x, l, c, s, d; least: p, -, k, j); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=3, L=4 & t=6.
